query_text: Tell me about some weird habits that some people have.

parts.text:
Humans are incredibly complex, and almost everyone has at least one or two strange habits that they keep secret—or didn’t even realize were "weird" until a friend, partner, or roommate pointed them out. 

From odd sensory preferences to subconscious coping mechanisms, here are some of the most common "weird" habits people have, categorized by how they manifest in daily life:

---

### 1. Sleep & Bedtime Rituals
* **"The Embalmed" Sleeper:** Some people sleep completely flat on their backs, perfectly straight, with their arms crossed over their chests like a mummy or a vampire in a coffin. They barely move an inch all night. While highly efficient, it can be deeply terrifying to roommates or partners who wake up in the middle of the night to check if they are still breathing!
* **The Thermostat Foot:** Many people cannot sleep without being covered by a heavy blanket, but they *must* stick exactly one foot or leg out from under the covers. Interestingly, there is science behind this: the soles of our feet have specialized blood vessels that help dump body heat, so sticking a foot out is a highly effective way for the brain to regulate core body temperature.
* **The "Anti-Monster" Shower Curtain Check:** Entering the bathroom and immediately pulling back the shower curtain to make sure no one is hiding in the tub—even in their own, locked apartment. 

### 2. The "Internal Theater" (Solitary Quirks)
* **Rehearsing Fake Arguments:** Standing in the shower or driving alone and having incredibly heated, highly articulate arguments with someone. People will plan exactly what they *would* say if a conflict arose, complete with dramatic hand gestures and facial expressions.
* **The Imaginary Interview:** Pretending to be a guest on a late-night talk show or a famous podcast. People will literally explain their mundane daily routines or life philosophies out loud to an imaginary interviewer while cooking dinner.
* **Narrating Your Own Life:** Speaking to oneself in the third person or narrating actions ("And now, he opens the cabinet to find the coffee..."). Psychologists actually note that this is a great way to boost cognitive focus and self-regulate under stress!

### 3. Food & Eating Oddities
* **The Sequenced Eater:** Refusing to let different foods on a plate touch. Furthermore, some people must finish one food item entirely before moving to the next. For example, they will eat all of their peas, then all of their mashed potatoes, and finally the chicken—never mixing flavors.
* **The Deconstructionist:** Eating foods by taking them apart first. This includes peeling the fried breading off chicken nuggets to eat it separately, licking the cream out of Oreos before eating the cookie, or eating a slice of pizza layer by layer (toppings, then cheese, then sauce, then crust).
* **Drinking Pickle Juice:** Finishing a jar of pickles and keeping the leftover brine in the fridge specifically to drink it like juice. (While it sounds bizarre, athletes actually do this to prevent muscle cramps due to the high sodium and electrolyte content!)

### 4. Tactile & Spatial Quirks
* **Avoid-the-Lines:** Walking down a sidewalk and actively adjusting your stride to avoid stepping on the cracks, or only stepping on tiles of a specific color inside a grocery store.
* **The Door Frame Tap:** Reaching up to slap or tap the top of a door frame every single time you walk through it. It’s an incredibly common subconscious physical twitch, especially among taller people.
* **Label Peeling:** Sitting at a bar or dinner table and slowly, meticulously peeling the paper label off a beer bottle, soda can, or water bottle until it is completely bare.

### 5. Daily Domestic Loops
* **The Fridge Spawn Check:** Walking to the kitchen, opening the refrigerator, staring blankly inside for 10 seconds, closing it, and then returning 5 minutes later to do the exact same thing. It’s not that they expect new food to have magically spawned; rather, it’s a subconscious search for entertainment or a transition ritual between tasks.
* **The Bag of Bags:** Keeping a designated drawer, cabinet, or one giant plastic bag that is tightly packed with hundreds of other plastic grocery bags "just in case." 

---

### Why do we have these habits?
Psychologists point out that many of these behavioral quirks are actually **self-regulatory behaviors**. Human brains love patterns, predictability, and control. When the outside world feels chaotic, repetitive little habits—like peeling a label, sleeping in a highly specific position, or sorting your food—give the brain a small, satisfying hit of order and comfort.
